labelers.rationale: Medical image registration ('alignment' in E1 sense) used as a capability test of MLLMs; AGI-generality premise but narrow single-task content (E3/E5), no generality-measurement method.
labelers.quote: We investigate this question through the task of medical image alignment assessment, where the goal is to establish whether there is anatomical correspondence between two images.

adjudication.rationale: E5/E3: a domain capability benchmark (MRI-PET and T1w-FLAIR registration QC) whose conclusion is about adopting MLLMs in medical-imaging pipelines; the AGI/generalist framing is a wrapper, with no generality-measurement method (I10) and no safety content, so wide premise / narrow content keeps it out.
adjudication.quote: These results support the use of MLLMs as part of medical imaging pipelines, providing evidence that these models can perform effective visual alignment assessments.
adjudication.adjudication_note: The full text (discussion and conclusion included) never turns the generality premise into a generality metric or any safety question; it stays a single-domain applied capability eval.

adjudication.rationale: Route A deployment: a frontier developer's release post states that agents run in OpenAI-managed sandboxes, built on the same sandboxing infrastructure as Codex and ChatGPT; under the release-post rule any stated safeguard suffices, and sandboxed agent code execution is a listed technique.
adjudication.quote: This leverages the same sandboxing infrastructure that powers Codex and ChatGPT.
adjudication.adjudication_note: Sandboxing gets several paragraphs (hosted sandbox, partner sandboxes, VPC deployment), not one passing mention, and it carries indirect evidence of what OpenAI deploys for Codex and ChatGPT, so the release-post rule's low bar is met; the infrastructure framing only lowers confidence.

adjudication.rationale: E8: a personal essay about learning a rhythm game, with reflective asides on learned versus engineered intelligence (Moravec's paradox, 'end-times'); it makes no alignment, safety or research-agenda argument, so it is not route B (I9) either.
